overview.title: Desk overview (morning brief, macro, energy)
overview.read: The morning brief (Wed Oct 21, 2026 02:54 PM ET) shows Class III milk down 0.59 cents (-3.3%), KC HRW wheat off 17.25 cents (-2.5%) and Chicago wheat down 15.00 cents (-2.3%). USDA’s weekly NDPSR dairy product prices release is scheduled for 12:00 PM ET today. A flash export sale in the past three days reported 114,000 MT of soybeans for delivery to China and 261,000 MT to unknown destinations for MY 2026/27. The desk’s strongest views are strongly bearish on corn and KC HRW wheat, while the macro backdrop is a -2 headwind across rates, dollar, Brazil real, MXN, risk, energy, China and breadth. Energy data show gas storage at 3,567 Bcf (week to 2026‑10‑09) and crude stocks at 412.5 mb, with the 3‑2‑1 crack at $51.97 /bbl, influencing farm fuel and ethanol margins.

faq.q: What matters most today?
faq.a: The key item today is the USDA NDPSR dairy product price release at 12:00 PM ET, which will set the tone for milk and other dairy contracts. Traders will also watch the continued weakness in Class III milk (-0.59 cents, -3.3%) and the sharp declines in KC HRW wheat (-17.25 cents, -2.5%) and Chicago wheat (-15.00 cents, -2.3%). The recent flash export sale of 114,000 MT of soybeans to China and 261,000 MT to unknown destinations adds a supply‑demand angle for soybeans.

faq.q: What is the macro backdrop for ags?
faq.a: The macro backdrop is a headwind with a score of -2, reflecting negative pressure across most factors. Rates are neutral (0), the dollar is negative, Brazil real is neutral (0), MXN is negative, risk is neutral (0), energy is positive, China is negative, and breadth is neutral. This combination of a firm dollar, high real yields and sticky inflation weighs on fund demand for commodities.

ZS.title: Soybeans
ZS.read: Soybeans (ZS) are trading at 1,246.25 ¢/bu on 2026-10-26, down 2.4% week‑over‑week and 6.0% month‑over‑month, with RSI at 34 and a weak ADX of 20. The desk rates the market neutral with low conviction because fundamentals are mildly bearish (ending stocks 315 M bu, stocks/use 6.9%, farm price $12.00) while flows are bullish (managed‑money net long 237,491 lots, near a 10‑yr long extreme) and technicals are mixed. Key price bands are 1,167.00 ¢/bu support and 1,256.50 ¢/bu resistance; a close above 1,279.64 ¢/bu (50‑day avg) would trigger trend‑follower buying, while below 1,227.27 ¢/bu (100‑day avg) adds selling. Upcoming catalysts include USDA weekly export sales on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-29 and the Crop Progress report on 2026-10-26, with the NASS Crop Production report due 2026-11-10.

faq.q: What is the desk's view and why?
faq.a: The desk view is neutral with low conviction because fundamentals are slightly bearish (ending stocks 315 M bu, stocks/use 6.9%, farm price $12.00) but flows are strongly bullish (managed‑money net long 237,491 lots, 99th percentile 10‑yr long) and technicals are mixed (sell daily, buy weekly, RSI 34). The disagreement among lenses leads to a small‑size, wait‑for‑confirmation stance.

faq.a: Managed‑money funds are net long 237,491 lots (17.9% of open interest), at the 99th percentile of a 10‑year long extreme, but they reduced net long by 14,169 lots this week, indicating fresh shorting pressure.

Price is at 628.25 ¢/bu (down 6.7% week, 12.4% month) in a mixed trend but technicals are strongly bearish (RSI 26, ADX 26, support 626.25, resistance 634.00).
